reason: The warm-condition signals reach the skin, where sweat glands can respond.
expectation: The signals should activate sweating as part of the cooling response.

effect: The warm signal produced liquid sweat; the cooling step still needs to be shown.
reaction: The distinction between sweat on the skin and evaporation is useful.
reason: Air at the skin is the likely next component for evaporating the sweat.
expectation: Sweat should evaporate into the air, carrying heat away from the skin.

effect: Evaporation cools the body, with less evaporation in humid air; the warm response may also involve skin vessels.
reaction: The distinction between producing sweat and evaporating it is clear.
reason: Warm signals and skin vessels suggest a second route for releasing heat.
expectation: The vessels should widen, increasing blood flow near the skin and heat loss to cooler air.

effect: Widening skin vessels completes the warm response by increasing heat transfer to cooler surroundings.
reaction: The heat-flow arrows make the vessel response clear.
reason: Cold signals reach the skin vessels, so their response is a direct way to investigate heat conservation.
expectation: The vessels should narrow, reducing blood flow near the skin and heat loss.

alternatives.reason: Cold signals also reach motor pathways and could trigger heat-producing muscle activity.

effect: Cold narrows skin vessels, reducing heat loss without producing new heat; muscle activity remains a likely cold response.
reaction: The distinction between conserving and producing heat is clear.
reason: Cold signals also reach skeletal motor pathways, suggesting a heat-producing response.
expectation: The signals should cause shivering, producing heat through muscle activity.

effect: Shivering completes the cold response by producing heat through repeated ATP-using contractions, distinct from conserving heat by narrowing vessels.
reaction: The contrast between heat production and conservation was satisfying and clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Comparing sweating with evaporation was most worthwhile: the planned pictures distinguish liquid sweat from actual heat loss and show why humidity matters.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial sweating result felt somewhat incomplete on its own, although the next step made its purpose clear.

surprise.text: The humid-air comparison made me think about how the surroundings limit evaporation, not just how much sweat the body produces.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary; each followed a visible signal or a physical connection in the planned pictures.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see more connected physiological responses, particularly if they preserve the clear contrasts between mechanisms shown here.
